_readme: Layouts are authored ONCE as ordered key lists. The grid mapping for landscape (5x3)
and portrait (3x5) is derived from this order, so nothing here is duplicated per
Each key: cmd = Fusion command id, label = text under the icon, match = the command's
display name in Fusion (used by scripts/resolve-commands.js to re-resolve ids against a
running Fusion -- ids are install-derived, never hand-invented).
page = open a sub-page. view = set a viewport property (Fusion has no command for these).
tab = switch Fusion's workspace/ribbon tab (no command for these either). text = raw text
command. peek = borrow another command's icon for a folder or tab key.
SLOTS 13, 14 AND 15 ARE A FIXED REGION. Every context page ends with the same three keys:
Tabs (the home/tab picker), View, and More (page 2 of this context) or Page 1 on a page-2.
They are three doors, not three commands, and they are the last three entries of every
page list because 13-15 is the only block that reads coherently in BOTH orientations --
the bottom row in portrait, the bottom-right cluster beside the dial in landscape.
All 15 keys are context keys. Globals (Undo, Redo) live in "aux" below, on the two side

A page marked "global": true is a door, not a sub-page -- it appears on every context and belongs to none. Global pages are excluded from the per-context memory, so returning to a context restores the folder you were in, never the fact that you had Tabs or View open.

aux._note: Undo and Redo sit on the two discrete side buttons, NOT on the dial: an encoder is easy to nudge while pressing it, and a stray rotation that silently undoes work is far worse than one that merely changes the camera. The dial gets the harmless job.

_rules_note: Ordered most specific first; the first match wins. Every tab id here was read off the
running Fusion via GET /tabs on 2026-07-28 and is recorded in docs/research/tab-dump.json.
Rules match on tab ID, never on tabName. The display names are not consistently cased --
ParaMeshOuterTab reports "Mesh", not "MESH" -- and they would change under a localised
Fusion. tabName survives only as a fallback on the tab-switch KEYS, where activate_tab tries
Form is matched on workspace, not tab: entering Create Form moves Fusion into its own

dashboard.title: No design open
dashboard._note: Fusion's start screen. Jamie on 2026-07-28: 'realistically, from the dashboard, you can't do any of the other functions'. Correct -- Sketch, Component, Measure, every tab key and every modelling command need a design open. Matched on workspace being null, NOT on hasDesign: read live off Jamie's Fusion while sitting on that screen, it reports workspace null but hasDesign TRUE, because an Untitled document exists behind the start screen. The first version of this rule used hasDesign and could never fire.

home.title: Fusion
home._note: The tab picker, and what the fixed Tabs key opens from anywhere. Deliberately has no fixed region of its own: this IS the navigation page, so a Tabs key here would point at itself and a More key would have nowhere to go. Row 1 is the five modelling tabs, row 2 the two remaining tabs plus the document actions, row 3 the rest.

keys.label: Axis Perp
keys.match: Axis Perpendicular to Face at Point

form.title: Form
form._note: Reached when Fusion enters the T-Spline environment. Confirmed live 2026-07-28: workspace TSplineEnvironment, tab FormTab.

utilities.title: Utilities
utilities._note: One page only, deliberately. Nothing here creates geometry -- it measures, checks or exports it -- and what would have gone on a page 2 (Curvature Map, Measure Alignment, component colour cycling, Show Text Commands) is once-a-year work that belongs in the ribbon. The More key therefore does not appear; slot 15 is Section instead.

view.title: View
view._note: Fusion exposes NO command definition for view orientation or visual style -- verified against a dump of all 3110 definitions. These keys use the add-in's "view" action, which sets the viewport directly. A keystroke sender cannot do this at all, which is why the add-in route exists.

dialog.title: Command
dialog._note: Shown whenever a Fusion command dialog is open. OK and Cancel go through text commands because there is no public API to press another command's buttons.

mesh.direct.title: Direct Mesh Editing
mesh.direct._note: Fusion's Direct Mesh Editing environment, entered from the mesh page's Direct Edit key. It was a trap before this page existed: the environment has its own Finish, the device fell through to the Solid page, and Finish Direct Edit sat on mesh.p2 where it could not be reached. Finish is therefore slot 1. Matched on tab id ALONE, without a workspace: ParaMeshBaseFeatureTab is unique across the 219 tabs in tab-dump.json, and it is not confirmed whether entering the environment moves Fusion into a different workspace the way Create Form does. Which commands Fusion actually enables in here is unverified -- the set below is the direct-editing subset of the mesh tools.
